# Arc API

<!-- Generated by `go run ./tools/apidoc` from internal/api. Don't edit by hand. -->

Arc's web app uses this API, and so can any other app. Most requests and responses are JSON;
media and live events use their documented content types. Start with [CLIENT-INTEGRATION.md](CLIENT-INTEGRATION.md)
for pagination, capabilities, playback and executable examples. The server's /docs/ page is an
interactive viewer of the generated OpenAPI contract.

## Versions

Apps should call **`/api/v1/...`**, the stable API: every endpoint below is there with `/api/`
replaced by `/api/v1/`. Endpoints won't be removed or changed incompatibly within v1 (new
fields and endpoints may appear, so ignore what you don't know). The unversioned `/api/...` paths
are the web app's and change with it. `GET /api/v1/health` answers with `api_version`.

## Signing in

The web app uses a cookie. Apps send a token instead: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

- **With the password**: `POST /api/v1/auth/login {"password", "device"}` → `{"token"}`. `device` is
  the app's name for itself (e.g. "Living Room Apple TV"), shown in Settings > Devices, where the
  admin can sign it out. Then pick a profile: `GET /api/v1/auth/status` lists them, and
  `POST /api/v1/auth/profile {"id", "pin"}` uses one.
- **A friend**: `POST /api/v1/auth/friend {"name", "password", "device"}` → `{"token"}`, already
  using their profile.
- **On a TV, with a code**: `POST /api/v1/auth/link {"device"}` →
  `{"code", "poll", "expires_in"}`. Show the code and ask the person to enter it in Arc (the profile
  menu's *Link a Device*, or `/link`). Meanwhile ask `GET /api/v1/auth/link/{poll}` every few
  seconds: 202 while waiting, then 200 with `{"token"}` once; 404 when the code has run out (10
  minutes).
- **At home**, when the admin allows it, profiles can be picked without signing in
  (`bypass` in `/auth/status`); the answer then sets a cookie.

## Errors

Failures answer with an HTTP error status and `{"error": "what went wrong, in plain words"}`,
sometimes with `needs` (e.g. `"pin"`, `"password"`, `"stopped"`) saying what to do next. 401 means
sign in (or choose a profile), 403 not allowed. Common JSON errors additionally include a stable
HTTP-category code and request_id, matching the server-issued X-Request-ID response header.
Older servers and plain-text transport errors may omit these fields; check HTTP status first.

## Playing

`POST /api/v1/items/{id}/playback` with what the player can play (`caps`) answers with a URL to play:
the file as it is, or an HLS stream Arc converts (keep it alive with `POST /transcode/{sid}/ping`).
Send progress with `PUT /items/{id}/progress`. Players that can't send the Authorization header
(e.g. a cast receiver) can turn that URL into a link with a token in it: `POST /api/v1/cast {"url"}`.

## Endpoints

211 endpoints, grouped by the first part of their path. **Who** is who may call it: `anyone`, any signed-in `profile`, or the `admin` profile.

### activity

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/activity` | admin | Lists what the server is doing now, and what it finished recently (newest first). |
| POST | `/api/activity/{id}/stop` | admin | Requests a stop for that cancellable task. |

### auth

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/auth/status` | anyone | Tells the web app what to show: first-run setup, the sign-in screen, the profile picker, or the app. |
| POST | `/api/auth/setup` | anyone | {"name", "password", "local_bypass", "tmdb_api_key", "tvdb_api_key"} creates the admin profile the first time AMS runs, and signs in as it. |
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | anyone | {"password"} signs in with the household password. A profile is picked next. |
| POST | `/api/auth/profile` | anyone | {"id", "pin", "password"} switches to a profile. A PIN is needed if the profile has one. On the home network without the password, the admin profile needs its PIN or the password, so no one else in the house can change settings. |
| DELETE | `/api/auth/profile` | anyone | Goes back to the profile picker. |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | anyone | Signs this browser out. |
| POST | `/api/auth/friend` | anyone | {"name", "password"} signs a friend in. |
| POST | `/api/auth/link` | anyone | {"device"} gives a TV a code to show, and a poll token to ask with whether it's been approved. |
| GET | `/api/auth/link/{poll}` | anyone | Answers 202 while the code waits, then once with {"token"} after it's approved; 404 when it has run out. |
| POST | `/api/auth/link/approve` | profile | {"code"} signs the TV showing the code in, as this household (it then picks a profile) or, for a friend, as them. The household needs the password to have been used here (or the admin profile), so someone at home without it can't give a device a sign-in that works away from home. |
| POST | `/api/auth/password` | admin | {"current", "new"} . Other browsers signed in with the old password are signed out. |

### capabilities

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/capabilities` | profile | Describes implemented API features, runtime availability and the selected profile's role permission. Item/library restrictions are still checked on every operation. Missing feature keys mean unsupported. Availability is a point-in-time hint, not a promise of provider/network/device compatibility; no credentials or paths are exposed. |

### cast

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/cast` | profile | {"url"} turns a stream URL from POST /api/items/{id}/playback into a link a cast device can open: absolute, at an address it can reach, with a token. It also takes a text subtitle track's WebVTT link (GET /api/items/{id}/subtitles/{track}/vtt) and an extra's stream link (GET /api/extras/{id}/stream). |
| GET | `/api/cast/{token}/{rest...}` | anyone | Serves a stream to a cast device. |
| OPTIONS | `/api/cast/{token}/{rest...}` | anyone | Serves a stream to a cast device. |

### discover

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/discover` | anyone | Lets an app on the home network find Arc without signing in: TV apps can't listen for broadcasts, so they try their network's addresses on Arc's port and list the servers that answer. Only answers requests from the home network (404 otherwise), and gives only the server's identity, name and version. |

### events

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/events` | profile | Is a profile-authenticated Server-Sent Events stream. "invalidate" hints identify a topic and optionally an allowed library, never titles/paths/item bodies. Personal hints only reach that profile; activity/sessions/maintenance are admin-only. "resync" requires refetching all client state. Send Last-Event-ID to resume; stale/process-restart cursors trigger resync. No tokens in URLs. Background catalog/artwork/optimized/previews/markers hints are cache invalidations, not job-success or playback commands. Max 32 streams/server and 8/profile; retries use 429 Retry-After. Heartbeats/revalidation every 10 seconds. |

|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/identity` | profile | Returns this server's persistent identity and friendly name. Requires a selected profile. Rename through PATCH /settings {"server_name":"Living room"}. ### items

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/theme` | profile | Plays a show's or movie's theme tune. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/preroll` | profile | Lists the pre-roll videos to play before a movie (none for episodes and home videos, or when none are set). |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/markers` | admin | Gives a movie's or episode's skip markers, where each came from, and the file's length. |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/markers` | admin | {"markers": [{"kind", "start_ms", "end_ms"}]} sets the markers by hand. Kinds left out have nothing to skip; found ones never replace these. |
| DELETE | `/api/items/{id}/markers` | admin | Forgets the markers, so they're found again from chapters, online and by detection. |
| POST | `/api/items/bulk` | admin | Changes many movies and shows at once: {"item_ids": [...], "add_genres": [...], "remove_genres": [...], "add_labels": [...], "remove_labels": [...], "content_rating": "15", "locks": "all" \| "none", "played": true, "refresh": true} Every field but item_ids is optional. "played" is for the current profile. "refresh" fetches their metadata again in the background (it shows in Activity). |
| POST | `/api/items/merge` | admin | {"target_id", "item_ids": [...]} makes several movies one, as versions of the target, or several shows one (store.MergeSeries), all from one library. Watch state, history and collections move with them. Shows must number their episode files the same way; merging them holds the library's work slot, then refreshes the kept show. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/split` | admin | Gives each version of a movie but the first its own title; they're identified at the scan that starts straight after. |
| GET | `/api/items/lookup` | profile | ?provider=tmdb\|tvdb\|imdb&provider_id=... returns all matching accessible identities. Optional kind=movie\|series\|episode, library_id, limit (1–100, default 50) and offset (0 or greater). Missing and restricted matches both produce an empty page. No provider request, scan or probe is started, and existing offline identities may be returned. |
| POST | `/api/items/batch` | profile | {"ids":[...]} retrieves up to 100 item details in requested order (duplicates retained). Unknown/restricted IDs are omitted identically, without missing counts. Same metadata/files/watch fields as individual item GET. This is read-only despite POST. |
| GET | `/api/items` | profile | Browse, filter and search. Sorts: title, added, year, release, rating, imdb, critics (Rotten Tomatoes), runtime, watched, shuffle (a new order each day). Set `reverse=1` to reverse a non-shuffle sort; paging uses a stable ID tie-breaker. Limit is 1–500 (default 100), offset 0–10000000; invalid or oversized bounds return 400. With title sort, `jump=A` through `Z` starts at that letter boundary in the same filtered list (or the next available title in the current direction). The response includes the full filtered `total` and actual `offset`; continue with `offset + items.length`, omitting `jump`. `letters=1` adds `letters`, the filtered titles counted by the first character of their sort title in A–Z order (`a`–`z`, `#` for anything else), so a client can tell where each letter starts. `unmatched=1` keeps titles Arc couldn't identify and shows with episodes it couldn't place. Resolutions: 4k, 1080, 720, sd. `language` is an original language (2-letter code). `added_within` is days, runtimes are minutes, `about` is comma-separated words to find in the title, tagline, description or TMDB keywords |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}` | profile | Item details with files and streams. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/stream` | profile | Serves the original file with HTTP range support (direct play). ?file=<id> selects a specific part or version; otherwise the first available file is used. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/playback-preview` | profile | Accepts the playback request and returns its decision without probing, starting a stream/conversion, changing playback state or preferences. No URL/session is allocated. Unanalysed files return needs_analysis=true. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/playback` | profile | {"caps": {...}, "file_id", "audio_stream", "start_ms"} decides how to play a movie or episode on this player and, unless it can play the file as it is, starts converting it. Starting again (e.g. to seek or change audio track) ends the player's previous conversion. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/playback-options` | profile | Resolves the edition/version and source track choices without starting a stream, conversion, progress or preference update. Send {"caps": {...}} and optionally "file_id" or "edition" as for playback. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles` | profile | ?file=<id> lists a file's subtitle tracks. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles/search` | admin | ?file=<id>&languages=en,fr finds subtitles online (OpenSubtitles) for a movie or episode, best first. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles/download` | admin | {"file": <id>, "result": <file_id>, "language", "forced", "hearing_impaired"} downloads a subtitle found online and keeps it in Arc's data folder (never beside the video), returning the new track. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles/{track}` | profile | ?file= returns a subtitle track's cues as JSON, for the web player to show. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles/{track}/vtt` | profile | ?file=&shift_ms= returns a text subtitle track as WebVTT, for a cast device to show itself. shift_ms moves every cue (negative is earlier): a converted stream's start point and the viewer's timing adjustment. Cues that end before 0 are left out. Cast devices fetch it through a cast link (see cast.go). Players wait for a subtitle file before they start the video, and reading a track out of a large video the first time takes minutes (the whole file is read). So the answer starts at once with the WebVTT header, stays alive with blank lines (which WebVTT allows between cues) while the track is read, then carries the cues: the video starts straight away and the subtitles follow. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/subtitles/{track}/ass` | profile | ?file=&shift_ms= returns an ASS/SSA track as its own script, for players that draw it with libass (keeping its fonts, colours, positions and effects): shifted as /vtt is, with the fonts the video carries packed into a [Fonts] section (up to 40 MB of them). Other tracks answer 400; use /vtt for those. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/trickplay` | profile | ?file=<id> describes a file's timeline thumbnails and where its sheets are. Until they're made it's 404, and the file moves up the queue. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/trickplay/{file}/{sheet}` | profile | Is one sheet of thumbnails. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/trickplay/{file}/bif` | profile | Is the same thumbnails as one BIF file, the format Roku's player shows while seeking. It's 404 until the thumbnails are made. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/images/{type}` | profile | Serves an item's artwork from the local cache, downloading it on first use. If it can't be downloaded (e.g. the provider is unreachable) the browser is sent to the provider instead. A backdrop with ?size=full is the full-resolution picture, for full-width banners. |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/progress` | profile | {"position_ms", "duration_ms"} from the player, every few seconds and on pause or close. |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/played` | profile | {"played": true} marks a movie or episode watched or unwatched for the current profile. For a series it applies to all its episodes, or with "season_number" to one season of the profile's episode order. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/next` | profile | Is the episode that follows one in the profile's episode order, for playing on: the next one on disk, staying out of specials unless the episode is one. 204 when there's none (the last episode, a movie, or an episode the order doesn't place). |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/similar` | profile | Is "More like this": movies or shows from the same library, TMDB's recommendations first, then titles sharing its collection, genres and cast. |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/rating` | profile | {"rating": 1-10, or 0 to clear} is the profile's own rating of a movie, show or episode (half stars out of five). |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/watchlist` | profile | {"on": true} puts a movie or show on the profile's watchlist, or takes it off. |
| DELETE | `/api/items/{id}` | admin | Forgets a movie, episode or show whose files are all gone (after backing up the database). Refused if any of its files is still there. |
| PATCH | `/api/items/{id}` | admin | Edits metadata (including genres and labels; labels are never locked); edited fields are locked. locked_fields replaces the locked set. For a show, source_ordering changes file numbering (empty follows the library). Show details use the library metadata provider; legacy details_provider inputs are rejected. Episode metadata follows file numbering. Display order is changed separately through the series API. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/refresh` | admin | Fetches metadata again now. Locked fields are kept. Episodes refresh their whole series. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/unmatch` | admin | Removes all metadata and artwork references, manual metadata overrides and display orders from a show and its episodes. Restores filename labels and file order, preserves IDs, files, source numbering, history, manual collections and playlists. Scans/refreshes keep it unmatched until an explicit Fix Match succeeds. No media, uploaded artwork files, probes or markers are deleted. Only series IDs are accepted. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/analyze` | admin | Rereads a movie's or episode's files, or every episode of a show. It runs in the background under the library's lease (stoppable from Activity) and keeps watch history, markers and edits. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/artwork` | admin | Lists the posters and backgrounds TMDB has for a movie or show, with the ones in use and whether they were chosen by hand. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/artwork/palette` | profile | Returns cached regional sRGB hex colours for a title's selected artwork (profile). ?type=backdrop (default) prefers a backdrop, falling back to primary only if no backdrop is configured; ?type=primary uses its poster/still. Missing or undecodable artwork answers 200 with available=false and a reason, never a theme-colour guess. |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/artwork` | admin | {"type": "poster", "path": "/abc.jpg"} uses a TMDB image and locks it. A null path goes back to automatic artwork. |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/artwork/{type}` | admin | With an image as the body (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 20 MB) uses it as the poster or background. It's kept in AMS's data folder. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/match` | admin | Explains how an item was identified: what was read from its file and folder names, and every search made with what it found. |
| GET | `/api/items/{id}/match/search` | admin | ?provider=tmdb&q=Alien&year=1979 |
| PUT | `/api/items/{id}/match` | admin | {"provider": "tmdb", "id": 603} identifies an item as the chosen provider entry and answers with the item. A movie's metadata is fetched before it answers. For a show it fetches only the chosen entry's own details and adds `match_task_id`: the Activity task fetching its seasons, episodes and episode orders in the background, which then links its files to the new episodes. The item keeps its previous match if the chosen entry can't be fetched. |

### libraries

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/libraries` | profile | Libraries with their size and scan status. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/scan` | profile | Scan progress. |
| POST | `/api/libraries/{id}/work` | admin | Starts {"operation":"refresh"\|"analyze"}. Refresh refetches known titles regardless of age; analyze rereads known present files, not folders. Both preserve locked metadata/history and share the library's scan/maintenance lease. |
| POST | `/api/libraries/{id}/stop` | admin | Stops {"job_id":...} only. It cancels queued follow-ups, never reconciles unvisited media, and leaves future triggers enabled. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/filters` | profile | Describes supported browsing and smart-row filter keys/types/operators. Enum values are supported choices, not availability counts. Fetch facets_url for access-controlled genre/language/label/decade/resolution availability. Media filters are source properties; audio/video constraints match one present file and one stream of each kind, including accessible child episodes for a series. Dynamic range precedence is Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HLG, HDR10, known SDR, unknown; this does not describe output capability. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/facets` | profile | Lists the genres, decades and resolutions a library's titles can be filtered by, with counts. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/collections` | profile | Lists a library's collections. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/folders` | profile | ?path= browses an Other videos library folder by folder: the folders inside path (none: the top) and the videos directly in it, oldest first. A library with several folders starts with one entry per folder. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/recent-shows` | profile | ?limit=24 is a TV library's newest additions, grouped by show: a show that's new appears once; several new episodes of a season appear as that season; a single new episode appears as itself. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/recommended/rows/{row}` | profile | ?limit=50&offset=20 continues a current visible row using its opaque id. Limit 1–100, offset 0–10000000. Missing/hidden/replaced daily rows return 404; refetch recommended to discover current IDs. Ordinary rows page their full filtered library; curated rows page at most 500 candidates (Continue Watching uses the existing 30 in-progress / 40 series windows). No provider calls. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/recommended` | profile | Is a library's Recommended view for the profile, in this order: Continue Watching (what it's part-way through here and the next episode of shows it's watching), Recently Released, Recently Added, Start Watching (shows not started), "Because you watched" rows for its recent titles, Top Rated, Recently Watched (episodes, in a TV library), Rediscover (finished more than six months ago), more of its favourite genres, the top titles of a genre and of an actor or director (both changing daily), and the best rated it hasn't seen. Each row has a type and parameters (name, genre, person_id, role) for the app to title in the viewer's language, plus an English title for apps written before rows had a type; rows without anything are left out. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/recommended/layout` | admin | Returns the library's shared row-family order, visibility and style . |
| PUT | `/api/libraries/{id}/recommended/layout` | admin | {"rows":[{"type","hidden","style"}]} sets shared Recommended rows . Empty rows resets defaults; omitted/new families remain visible. Styles: poster, thumb, arc or empty for automatic. |
| POST | `/api/libraries` | admin | {"name", "kind", "paths", "source_ordering"} adds a library and starts scanning it. |
| PATCH | `/api/libraries/{id}` | admin | {"name", "paths", "source_ordering", "trickplay"} changes a library (not its kind) and rescans it. |
| DELETE | `/api/libraries/{id}` | admin | Removes a library and everything AMS knows about it, after backing up the database. Media files aren't touched. |
| POST | `/api/libraries/{id}/scan` | admin | Starts a scan. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/unmatched` | admin | Lists items that need attention. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/health` | admin | Reports everything in a library worth a look: unidentified items, unreadable, unrecognised and missing files, duplicates and missing episodes. watch_problem describes failed folder notifications and the configured scheduled fallback. |
| GET | `/api/libraries/{id}/markers` | admin | Lists the library's shows and movies with how many of their files have intro and credits markers and how many have been checked, for Library Health. |
| POST | `/api/libraries/{id}/compatibility` | admin | {"caps": {...}} says how a library's titles would play on a player that can play those things: how many directly, repackaged or converted, why, and which titles need converting. |
| POST | `/api/libraries/{id}/empty-trash` | admin | Forgets everything in a library whose files are gone (after backing up the database). Media files aren't touched. ?safe=1 additionally requires fresh complete-scan proof and readable unchanged roots; unsafe/busy libraries return a skipped reason. |

### play-queues

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/play-queues` | profile | Creates this device/profile's queue from item_ids (movies, episodes or expanded shows) or playlist_id. Playlist contents are snapshotted. Replacing an existing queue requires replace_id and revision. Up to 1000 entries including duplicates. Does not start/stop playback or change watched state. |
| GET | `/api/play-queues/{id}` | profile | Retrieves only this device/profile's queue. The id "current" recovers it after app restart. Queues expire after seven inactive days. Restricted or missing entries retain opaque entry IDs but expose no item IDs or metadata. |
| PATCH | `/api/play-queues/{id}` | profile | Requires revision and operation: append/next with item_ids; remove/reorder with entry_ids; select with entry_id; clear, advance, shuffle or unshuffle. Reorder protects the current/past prefix; clear drops upcoming entries. Queue position changes never remotely control a player; clients start/stop playback separately. |
| DELETE | `/api/play-queues/{id}` | profile | ?revision=<revision> deletes this device/profile's queue. The client stops its own player separately. Session revocation also deletes queues. |

### series

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/series/{id}/seasons` | profile | ?ordering=<id>&missing=1 Arranges the series' episodes by an ordering (the display ordering by default). Episodes you have that the ordering doesn't place are returned in "unplaced" rather than hidden. |
| GET | `/api/series/{id}/seasons/{n}/image` | profile | Is a season's poster: the file in the show's folder if there is one, otherwise the provider's. |
| GET | `/api/series/{id}/orderings` | profile | Available orderings and the one in use. |
| PUT | `/api/series/{id}/display-ordering` | admin | {"ordering_id": 12} (null goes back to the file order) sets the order a series is shown in, for everyone. Choosing an ordering from the other provider triggers a thorough episode mapping first. |
| PATCH | `/api/series/{id}/specials` | admin | {"inline_specials": true\|false\|null} (null is Off) places specials between regular episodes, for everyone. This changes display/playback traversal only; manual/custom placements and original numbering remain authoritative. |
| POST | `/api/series/{id}/orderings` | admin | {"name": "...", "copy_from": <ordering id>} creates a custom ordering starting as a copy of another. |
| DELETE | `/api/series/{id}/orderings/{oid}` | admin | (custom orderings only) |
| PUT | `/api/series/{id}/orderings/{oid}/entries/{eid}` | admin | {"season_number": 1, "episode_number": 5} Manually positions an episode. Manual positions survive metadata refreshes. |
| DELETE | `/api/series/{id}/orderings/{oid}/entries/{eid}` | admin | Removes a manual position; provider orderings restore their own on the next refresh. |
| POST | `/api/series/{id}/refresh` | admin | ?deep=1 re-fetches metadata and orderings now. |
| GET | `/api/series/{id}/season-art` | admin | Lists a show's seasons (in aired order, which season posters belong to) with the poster each uses. |
| PATCH | `/api/series/{id}/seasons/{n}` | admin | ?ordering=<id> {"name", "overview", "locked_fields"} changes a season's name and summary in an episode order (the show's display order by default). Fields sent are locked so refreshes keep them; "locked_fields" replaces the locked set. |
| GET | `/api/series/{id}/seasons/{n}/artwork` | admin | Lists the posters TMDB has for a season. |
| PUT | `/api/series/{id}/seasons/{n}/artwork` | admin | {"path": "/abc.jpg"} uses a TMDB poster for a season; a null path goes back to automatic. |
| POST | `/api/series/{id}/seasons/{n}/artwork` | admin | With an image as the body uses it as the season's poster. |

### watch-together

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/watch-together` | profile | {item_id,start_ms} creates a paused room and an expiring readable invite code. Up to 20 rooms/server, 10 participants/room, one active room per device/profile. Existing signed-in household profiles and friends are allowed. No stream starts. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/join` | profile | {code} joins an unexpired invite only if the profile may play the current movie/episode. Wrong, expired and restricted invites all return 404. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/time` | profile | ?client_sent_ms=... echoes an optional integer client timestamp and server receive/send epoch milliseconds for midpoint/RTT clock estimation. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/current` | profile | Recovers only this device/profile's own active membership (404 if none). Use after reload or a lost create/join response; never lists rooms. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/people` | profile | ?item_id= lists who this profile may invite, and whether each may play the title. Names and colours only. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/rooms` | profile | Lists the rooms this profile made, was invited to or is in, newest first, for Home's Watch Together row. Rooms whose title it may not play are left out. Rooms are private: nobody else's appear. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/rooms` | profile | {item_id,start_ms,profile_ids} makes a room for the chosen people: nobody is in it until they join from their room lists (the host too). It waits an hour for them. Each person must be someone this profile may invite (GET .../people) and may play the title. The code is returned as for any room. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/rooms/{id}/join` | profile | Joins a room from this profile's list (no code), if it may play the room's title. Returns the personalized room. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/rooms/{id}/dismiss` | profile | Takes a room off this profile's list. Someone invited declines; the profile that made it cancels it for everyone. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/{id}/people` | profile | {profile_ids} invites more people to a room (host only, members only). Returns the personalized room with them in `invited`. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/{id}` | profile | Returns a member-only personalized timeline. A member denied a changed title remains present with available:false and no item/id metadata. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/{id}/leave` | profile | Leaves this device/profile only. The oldest remaining participant inherits host control. Personal playback/history is untouched. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/{id}/commands` | profile | {revision,action,position_ms,item_id}. Actions play/pause/seek/change_item are shared controls; only the host may end. Seek and item changes increment generation so readiness for older media/positions cannot release the barrier. A stale revision returns 409 with the current personalized room. No playback session is created. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/{id}/heartbeat` | profile | {generation,position_ms,state,ready} reports presence/readiness, never changes shared position or watch history. Up to four reports/second. Waiting defaults to ten seconds, then slow viewers catch up themselves. A stale seek/title generation returns 409 with current room state. |
| POST | `/api/watch-together/{id}/invite` | profile | {revision} creates a fresh 15-minute code (host only), invalidating the old one. Codes are returned only at create/renew, never in GET. |
| GET | `/api/watch-together/{id}/events` | profile | Is a private room SSE stream carrying full personalized room snapshots (event: room, id: revision). It does not consume /events slots. One stream/member (a reconnect replaces the older one), at most 200/server; initial/reconnect always sends the latest snapshot. Changes wake immediately; timeout transitions are checked every 200ms. Auth/access are freshly checked before each payload and at least every two seconds; revoked/switched sessions close. No tokens/codes in URLs. Thirty-minute streams, five-second write deadlines, no event queues. |
